warpScale.description: Metres per lobe of coastline wobble. Small values fray the coast into inlets; large ones bend the whole landmass.

coastVariation.description: How much `falloff` varies around the coast, as a fraction. 0.6 means some stretches of shore descend over 40% of the band (steep: headlands and sea cliffs) and others over 160% (gentle: beaches and shallow bays). This is what gives one island a beach on one side and cliffs on the other.

coastVariationScale.description: Metres per cycle of the falloff variation — how long a stretch of cliff or beach coast is.

lobes.description: Extra discs [dx, dz, radius], relative to `center`, smoothly UNIONED with the main one. This is what stops a continent being a circle: two or three lobes make a crescent, an L, a landmass with a peninsula and a gulf. Each lobe still gives an exact distance to its shore, so the shore profile and the land floor hold everywhere.

lobeBlend.description: Metres over which lobes merge into one another instead of meeting at a crease. Wider = softer bays where they join.

frequency.description: Cycles per world unit. 0.0008 = continents, 0.01 = hills, 0.08 = rocks.

amplitude.description: World units this band contributes (ridged bands run 0..amplitude, others +/-amplitude).

ridged.description: Sharp crests, flat valleys — the difference between rolling hills and a mountain range.

seed.description: Added to the world seed so two identically-tuned bands still differ.

erosion.description: Slope-weighted octaves: fine detail is damped where the band is already steep, so valleys come out smooth and walkable while ridgelines stay crisp. This is the single biggest lever against terrain that reads as jagged noise — plain fBm puts the same 30 m crinkle on every slope in the world. 0.3-0.6 on the mountain band; costs ~40% more per octave (derivative noise).

crest.description: Ridged bands only: round the crests. The ridged fold puts a knife-edge crease at every ridgeline and summit of every octave, and the voxel mesh renders each one as a corner it cannot smooth — the 'cliffs that come to a sharp edge at the top'. 0 (default) keeps the crease; 0.2 rounds each crest over about a fifth of the band's swing without moving the summit line. Free.

cliff.description: How much steeper the land gets at the waterline where the coast noise says 'rugged'. 0 makes every shore a beach, which is the failure this fixes: a height-band beach rule applied to a uniformly gentle coastline rings the entire world in one unbroken strip of sand.

band.description: World units above and below sea level the steepening reaches. Roughly the height of the headlands.

frequency.description: How often the coast alternates between cliff and cove.

amplitude.description: World units of dune crest. 0 disables the band entirely, and with it the extra climate lookup per column.

stretch.description: Elongation across the prevailing wind. 1 is lumps; 3-4 is the long parallel ridges that read as sand.

angle.description: Wind direction in radians — the axis the ridges run along.

amplitude.description: World units of table height. 0 disables the band.

steps.description: Strata per table: each is a riser and a tread.

sharpness.description: How square the risers are. 0 is a smooth dome.

height.description: The highest the ground can be, asymptotically. Peaks approach it and never reach it.

softness.description: Metres below `height` at which the compression begins. Wider = gentler summits.

step.description: Metres of altitude per terrace — the height of one riser, and roughly the height of one cliff band.

sharpness.description: How square the riser is. 0 leaves the slope untouched; 0.72 spends ~28% of each band's altitude on the riser and flattens the rest into a tread. Past ~0.9 the riser is vertical enough that the voxel lattice, not this number, is what limits it.

strength.description: How much of the terraced profile to blend in where the mask is full. Below 1 the risers soften back toward the raw slope.

rounding.description: Fraction of each riser's height spent easing into the tread at its top and foot, instead of meeting it at a crease. 0 is the raw clamp — a riser that hits the tread at a corner, which the mesh renders as a knife edge along every cliff top. 0.25 rounds the crest and the foot over a quarter of the riser each while the middle half stays as sheer as `sharpness` asks.

minBands.description: How many `step` bands of mountain relief a place must have before it is terraced at all, fading in over the next 1.4 bands. This is what keeps cliffs ON MOUNTAINS: without it the edge of the mountain band — a hillock with one band's worth of height — gets a single enormous step, which reads far harsher than the mountain itself does because there is no mountain around it to explain it, and it is visible from a long way off.

mask.description: WHERE the terracing happens. Without this every mountain in the world is terraced from base to summit and reads as a ziggurat, which is not what a mountain range looks like — a range is mostly smooth flank with cliff bands breaking out of it here and there. Widen the start..end gap for cliffs that fade in; raise `start` for rarer, more dramatic ones.

jitter.description: Metres the band boundaries wander from place to place. Without it every terrace in the world is a perfectly level contour ring at the same altitude, which reads as a contour map rather than as rock.

frequency.description: Cycles per world unit. 0.0012 is a cliff band a few hundred metres across.

start.description: Mask value at which terracing begins to appear.

end.description: Mask value at which it is in full.

strength.description: World units the surface can bulge horizontally. 0 = a pure heightfield.

slopeStart.description: Only steep ground gets overhangs — flat fields must stay walkable.
Steepness at which the tunnel network may start reaching the surface.

slopeEnd.description: Steepness at which it fully may.

minDepth.description: The `minDepth` that applies on fully steep ground. NEGATIVE means tunnels are allowed to push past the surface, which is what actually cuts an opening; at 0 they only ever kiss it.

warp.description: World units the climate field is domain-warped by before it is read. This is the LARGE-scale raggedness: it makes a desert reach a peninsula into the meadow instead of ending on a smooth curve.

strength.description: Fine noise (in the climate's own 0..1 units) added to temperature and moisture. This is the SMALL-scale raggedness: it breaks the last few metres of every border into speckle, so the transition is a scatter of blighted ground in the grass rather than a line.

heightJitter.description: World units of noise added to the ground height that HEIGHT windows are tested against — the same trick for the snowline and the beach, which are height-driven rather than climate-driven.

size.description: Mean zone diameter in metres. A region should take minutes to cross, not seconds.

jitter.description: How far each zone's site wanders from its grid point. 0 is a checkerboard.

warp.description: Metres the zone borders are pushed around by noise, so they read as coastlines rather than as cell walls.

border.description: Width of the blend between two zones, in metres. Biome rules still see a gradient across it.

strength.description: How strongly zones sort by latitude. 0 = anchors are picked by weight alone.

scale.description: Metres from the cold pole to the hot one, centred on the origin along `axis`.

seed.description: Added to the world seed for the zone layout alone, so the layout can be re-rolled without moving a single hill. Which anchor a zone gets is a draw, and a small world can draw no desert at all: a generator that needs every kind of place can sweep this until each anchor covers real land.

weight.description: How often zones pick this anchor, relative to the others.

latitude.description: Preferred latitude band, 0 = the cold pole, 1 = the hot pole (see `climate.zones.latitude`). A zone picks anchors by weight TIMES how close its own latitude is to this, so tundra collects at one end of the world and jungle at the other instead of both being sprinkled everywhere. Omit = anywhere.

relief.description: Multiplies the MOUNTAIN band here. 1 = a mountain zone; 0 = no peaks at all.

hills.description: Multiplies the hills band. 0 = a plain; 1.5 = broken country.

dunes.description: Multiplies the dune band (`terrain.dunes`) here. 1 = a dune sea.

mesas.description: Multiplies the mesa band (`terrain.mesas`) here. 1 = badlands: terraced tables and buttes.

flatten.description: Pulls the continent band down toward the land floor. 1 = a low, level plain hugging the waterline — swamp ground.

name.description: Human/AI-facing label: grass, sand, rock, snow.

color.description: Tint, and the whole appearance until a texture is supplied.

map.description: Texture asset id (assets/textures/) — albedo, projected triplanar.

blend.description: Softness of the temperature/moisture/slope window edges, in those windows' own 0..1 units.

heightBlend.description: Softness of the `height` window edges, in WORLD UNITS — height is the one window measured in metres, so it needs its own blend or a 0.08 softness makes a razor edge across a hillside.

weight.description: Relative pull where several rules match equally.

cliffStart.description: Steepness at which `cliff` starts replacing `surface`, in sin(angle). 0.57 is 35 degrees, roughly the angle of repose: past it soil and sand stop staying put, which is why cover gives way to rock there. These are authored against `slope()` units, so anything that measures steepness differently silently means a different ANGLE here.

cliffEnd.description: Steepness at which `cliff` fully replaces `surface`. 0.82 is 55 degrees.

tint.description: Multiplied over the blended surface color — cheap per-biome variation.

zones.description: Zone anchor ids (`climate.zones.anchors[].id`) this rule belongs to. The rule's membership is multiplied by the blended zone weight, so a rule listed here exists ONLY inside those zones — which is how a blighted region and a badland can both be hot-and-dry without fighting over the same climate corner. Omit for a rule that applies wherever its climate/height/slope windows say.

label.description: Does this rule NAME the place? Cover-only rules — a crag rule that paints bare rock on steep ground in every biome — must set false. `biome().id` is the strongest rule by membership, and everything that asks 'which biome is this' reads it: scatter's `biomes` filter above all. A cover rule left labelling quietly renames every slope in the world, and the pines filtered to "meadow" stop appearing on hills.

surface.description: Palette surface NAME to lay down (matched case-insensitively).

biomes.description: Biome ids this may appear in; empty = anywhere. The gate is the biome's blended membership, so patches fade out across a border instead of stopping at it.

frequency.description: Cycles per world unit. 0.02 ~ 50 m blotches.

threshold.description: Noise level (-1..1) at which the patch starts. Higher = rarer, smaller patches.

blend.description: Noise range over which it fades in. Small = hard-edged scabs, large = soft mottling.

strength.description: How completely the patch replaces the ground under it at full mask. 1 = bare.

slope.description: Restrict to a steepness window — dirt worn through on flat ground, scree only on slopes.

mode.description: Two different motions, not one with a knob. `sway` BENDS the whole plant from a base pinned to the ground - displacement grows with height, so it leans as one piece. That is a bush or a reed. `ripple` shivers each leaf card on the spot with NO net lean, phase varying across the model so cards move against each other: the canopy shimmers while the tree stands still, which is what real timber does in a light wind. Putting `sway` on a tree is the classic mistake - the trunk swings like a blade of grass and the model reads as rubber.

strength.description: Peak displacement in METRES of world space, not a fraction of the model. A ripple wants 0.02-0.06; a bush sway 0.08-0.2.

canopy.description: `ripple` only: fraction of the model height where the canopy starts. Everything below is held perfectly still, which is how the trunk stays out of it. It is a HEIGHT test rather than a 'is this the leaf material' test on purpose: Blockbench exports every material as alphaMode MASK, so a cutout test catches the trunk too (the same trap `foliageNormals` documents), while height does not care where the trunk sits horizontally.

materials.description: Only move materials whose NAME, or whose colour texture's name, contains this (case-insensitive) — `leaves` for a model whose leaf texture is called Leaves. The rest of the model stands still and the `canopy` height test is skipped, so the trunk stays put by NAME rather than by height. Name the texture or material in the DCC tool before export: Blockbench exports a pasted texture as literally 'pasted', which matches nothing, and an unmatched model gets no wind at all.

stack.description: How many props down one column, picked per lattice point. The stack stops early where the face does.

spacing.description: Metres of drop between one prop and the next. Set it under the model's height so they overlap and read as one mass.

spacingJitter.description: How much each step may vary, as a fraction of `spacing`.

embed.description: Depth pushed INTO the face along its inward normal, in MODEL units — it is multiplied by the instance scale, like `yOffset`, so resizing a prop does not leave it hanging off the wall. This is the field that decides whether the prop looks bolted onto the cliff or part of it; roughly a third of the model's depth is a good start.

embedJitter.description: Random variation on `embed`, in the same model units.

lateral.description: Metres each prop may slide sideways along the face, so a column is not a plumb line of rocks.

faceOut.description: How strongly each prop turns to face out of the cliff. 1 = square to the face, 0 = free yaw (the ordinary scatter behaviour).

yawSpread.description: Radians of random yaw either side of the outward direction. This plus `tilt` is what stops a stack looking like one model copy-pasted.

tilt.description: Radians of random tilt off vertical, about a random horizontal axis.

lean.description: Radians the prop tips BACK into the face (negative tips it out). A cliff recedes as it rises, so an upright prop bedded at its base has its top hanging in open air — which is exactly what makes a face read as planted menhirs instead of rock. Roughly `atan(model height / (2 x embed))` cancels it. This is NOT `alignToNormal`: that one lays a prop ONTO a slope, which on a cliff leans it further out.

minDrop.description: The face must fall at least this far below the lattice point for the column to start at all. Guards against decorating every short steep bank in the world.

search.description: Metres to march outward looking for the face at each step's height. Wider catches gentler faces, and it is the per-instance cost knob — but it is also how far a prop can end up from the lattice point that owns it, so keep it WELL under a quarter of `cellSize` or a cell starts emitting props that live in its neighbour and pop when it unloads.

__schema147.description: World-space XZ control points; the feature is the polyline through them.

depth.description: How far below the surrounding land the floor sits.

rim.description: Horizontal distance the walls take to climb back to natural terrain.

steps.description: Terraces in each wall. 1 is a smooth ramp; 3-4 reads as bedded rock.

stepSharpness.description: 0 = the terraces vanish into a straight slope, 1 = vertical risers and flat treads.

polygon.description: World-space XZ outline of the shore. Omit for a disc of `radius` about `center`.

waterY.description: Surface height. The basin is carved to sit below it; land outside the outline is untouched past `bank`.

depth.description: How far below the surface the deepest water is.

bank.description: Distance over which the shore eases from the waterline back to natural terrain, and the bed from the shore down to `depth`.

carve.description: true (hand-placed lakes): dig the basin — everything inside the outline goes down to `depth`, and a `bank` outside it eases to the waterline, whatever the ground was. false (`worldgen rivers` writes this): the terrain already holds the basin the hydrology found, so only ground at or under the surface is deepened, blended over two banks, and ground standing over a metre above it — an island, or an outline that overshot onto a hillside — is left alone. Carving a traced outline dug craters with vertical walls where it strayed uphill.

material.description: Water material for THIS lake, overriding the recipe's `waterMaterial`. A swamp pool is still, murky and opaque; a tarn is clear — one water for both reads wrong in both.

surface.description: Palette surface NAME painted on the bed and a `shore` band around the outline — wet sand, gravel — so the ground under and beside the water is not the biome's grass. Empty leaves the biome's cover; an unknown name paints nothing.

shore.description: Metres beyond the outline the `surface` fades out over.

points.description: World-space XZ of the two abutments: where the road stops on one bank and resumes on the other.

deckY.description: Height of the deck surface; the roads on both banks end at this height.

waterY.description: Water surface under the span, for the WFC stage to size piers.

material.description: Material for the deck, overriding the recipe's `bridgeMaterial`.

polygon.description: World-space XZ outline of the hollow.

y.description: Height the floor is raised to: the hollow's spill level, a little over.

bank.description: Distance beyond the outline over which the raise eases out.

points.description: World-space XZ, head first, mouth last.

points.description: World-space path in 3D — unlike rivers and roads, a cave goes up and down as well as along.

radius.description: Passage radius. endRadius.description: Radius at the last point; omit for a uniform tube. Lets a passage open out into a chamber.

above.description: World units of air polygonized above the highest ground in a cell — headroom for overhangs and arches.

below.description: World units of rock polygonized below the lowest ground in a cell. This is what makes surface caves enterable, and it is THE vertical cost knob: it multiplies both the sampled volume AND the cave surface the mesher has to triangulate, so it hits twice. Deeper cave networks want vertical chunk sections, not a bigger band here.

scale.description: World units per cycle of the broad band.

strength.description: Brightness swing, plus and minus. 0 disables the whole overlay.

detailScale.description: Second band, near tile size (10-20). This is the one that hides the grid up close.

colorStrength.description: How far the overlay shifts COLOUR, per channel, on top of the brightness swing. Brightness alone makes a large area read as one material under uneven light; letting the channels drift apart slightly — warmer here, greyer there — is what reads as the ground actually being different from place to place. 0.06-0.15 is a natural mottle; past ~0.25 the terrain goes tie-dye.

colorScale.description: World units per cycle of the colour band. Defaults to `scale`. Set it larger for broad regional colour shifts that survive being seen from a distance.

warp.description: How far the texture PROJECTION is pushed around by noise before it is sampled, as a fraction of each layer's OWN tile, so one setting means the same thing to a 3.5m grass tile and a 9m cliff tile. This is the one that actually kills tiling: brightness noise can only shade OVER a grid, and the grid is still underneath it — on a big flat-lit face seen from a distance the eye finds it anyway. warpScale.description: World units per cycle of the warp. Measured: keep it near TWICE the tile size, not far above it. A warp much coarser than the tile slides whole tiles around and leaves the motif inside each one perfectly intact, so a strongly patterned texture still reads as a pattern; a warp at roughly tile scale distorts the motif itself, which is what stops a big rock face looking stamped.

count.description: Copies played. 1 = the module plays once.

every.description: Seconds between copies — the STEP. Nothing tweens between them; each copy appears whole.

step.description: Metres each copy moves on from the last, in the spell frame (x right, y up, z forward): [0,0,1.4] marches spikes away from the caster, [0,0.5,0] stacks rings into a column.

turn.description: Degrees each copy is turned around the anchor's up axis relative to the last. With `step` [0,0,r] and turn 360/count the copies stand in a circle; on an orbiting sprite it advances the orbit phase instead.

alternate.description: Flip the spin (and a slash's tilt) on every other copy — a column of circles turning against each other.

scale.description: Size multiplier applied per copy: 0.85 tapers a stack, 1.3 steps a shockwave outward.

jitter.description: Metres of seeded horizontal scatter added to each copy.

spread.description: Half-angle, in degrees, that each particle's launch direction is randomised within — on ANY shape, unlike coneAngle. 0 fires every particle along `direction` in exact parallel, which is right for a jet and wrong for anything suspended: a box of specks all falling parallel reads as SNOW. 180 is a full sphere, the usual choice for dust hanging in the air.

turbulenceSpeed.description: How fast the wander field evolves. Low (~0.2) is a lazy indoor drift; high is agitated.

fadeIn.description: Fraction of each particle's life spent ramping up from nothing to `opacityStart`. radial.description: Aim each particle along the line from the emitter's centre to its own spawn point instead of along `direction`: out = an explosion (needs a sphere/box shape so there IS an offset); in = energy CONVERGING on the centre — the charge-up look, particles born on the shell and flying inward. `spread` still scatters around that line.

sprite.description: The procedural sprite used when no `texture` is given: soft = a radial falloff (smoke, glow); square = a hard-edged square with a one-texel fade (PSX sparks and rain); pixel = a chunky 6x6 blob with stepped alpha (retro embers, motes).

subUV.description: Play the texture as a SPRITE SHEET, per particle. A still sprite drifting is the clearest tell that an effect is dated — every modern smoke, fire or impact particle animates on its own clock.

softFade.description: Metres over which a particle fades as it approaches solid geometry. 0 = off. A quad slicing visibly into the ground is THE thing that reads as cheap, and nothing else fixes it. sizeCurve.description: [[t, size], …] over normalized life, overriding sizeStart/sizeEnd. A two-point lerp cannot describe a flash — spike, fast falloff, long dim tail — which is most of what separates an impact from a fading blob.

opacityCurve.description: [[t, opacity], …] over normalized life, overriding opacityStart/End and fadeIn.

space.description: world = particles trail behind a moving emitter; local = they ride it.

sizeCurve.description: [[t, size], …] over normalized life, overriding sizeStart/sizeEnd. A two-point lerp cannot describe a flash — spike, fast falloff, long dim tail — which is most of what separates an impact from a fading blob.

opacityCurve.description: [[t, opacity], …] over normalized life, overriding opacityStart/End and fadeIn.

space.description: world = particles trail behind a moving emitter; local = they ride it.

ground.description: Terrain contact. The host answers 'how high is the ground here' from the streamed terrain, sampled once per particle at birth; a particle that falls to it dies or settles. Terrain only — props, roofs and water are not tested. Needs space: world. Settled particles count toward `max`, so a settling snowfall wants a large one.

mode.description: life = play the sheet once across the particle's lifetime (smoke that billows and dissipates); loop = play it repeatedly at `fps`; random = hold one frame chosen per particle, which is the cheap way to make a hundred identical quads stop looking identical.
kill = the particle ends on contact (a raindrop); settle = it stops where it landed, holds, then fades (snow).

hold.description: settle only: seconds a landed particle rests before fading.

fade.description: settle only: seconds the fade-out takes.

offset.description: Height above the ground a landed particle rests at.

splash.description: Entity id (or tag) of another emitter to burst ONE particle from at the contact point — a raindrop's splash. That emitter usually has rate 0.

theme.description: A theme data asset: the complete per-location skin. One dungeon plan + N themes = N locations. Generate the engine material docs from it with materialsForTheme(); resolve mesh world-UV scales with uvScaleFor().

__schema0.description: Human-readable theme name, e.g. "The Ossuary Vaults".

__schema1.description: One or two sentences of art direction — what this location should feel like.

__schema3.description: The colours this theme's light fixtures CAST — part of the dressing vocabulary, not the layout. Dressing passes read these when placing lights so a re-skin changes the light along with the walls.

__schema4.description: Colour cast by this theme's warm fixtures (torches, braziers, hearths).

__schema6.description: Colour cast by this theme's cold sources (moonlight shafts, fungus, sorcery).

__schema7.description: Colour cast by accent-slot fixtures (runes, crystals, shrines) — pairs with the `accent` slot.

__schema8.description: Role slot → texture set. Compilers and dressing passes reference SLOTS, never material ids, so swapping the theme re-skins everything built from the same plan.

__schema9.description: Walkable worked surfaces — room floors, corridor floors.

__schema10.description: Texture asset id — the relative path under assets/textures/ INCLUDING extension (e.g. "crypt-a/mossy-brick-wall.png"), which is how the asset loader keys textures. Omit for a flat-colour slot (graybox, or a slot this location genuinely leaves untextured).

__schema12.description: Base colour, multiplied with `map` when one is set (leave #ffffff to show the texture untinted; darken it to grime a whole slot). With no `map` this IS the slot's look.

__schema13.description: PBR roughness 0..1. Omitted = engine material default (0.85, near-matte — right for stone). Set it low only on slots that should read wet or polished.

__schema15.description: PBR metalness 0..1. Omitted = engine material default (0.05). Really only the `metal` slot wants a high value; metallic stone reads as oily.

__schema17.description: Texture asset id of a tangent-space normal map (OpenGL +Y convention), same id form as `map`. Shares `map`'s UV transform, so the theme's single `uvScale` covers both.

__schema19.description: METRES PER TEXTURE TILE [u, v] in world space — NOT a UV repeat count. [3, 3] = one tile every 3 m. REQUIRED whenever `map` is set: the shell materials generated from a theme pin `repeat` to [1, 1] and the mesh carries `uv: { mode: "world", scale }` instead, so this value is what keeps a re-skin from silently changing the texture's world size (the counting-stones bug). Compilers read it with `uvScaleFor(theme, slot)` and bake it into the mesh they emit.

__schema22.description: One role slot: which texture set a semantic surface role wears in this theme, plus the metres-per-tile that keeps its world scale stable across re-skins.

__schema24.description: Overhead shell surfaces — flat ceilings and vault faces.

__schema25.description: Carved edging: door frames, cornices, balustrades, pilasters — the detail band between shell slots.

__schema26.description: The theme's signature flourish — runes, bone, glow, gilt. Small doses; pairs with light.accent.

__schema27.description: Natural/unworked stone — cave walls, tunnel shells, rubble, stalagmites. The other half of the worked/natural mix; transition assemblies blend wall→rock.

__schema28.description: Structural and prop timber — beams, planking, crates, scaffolds.

__schema29.description: Ironmongery — grates, hinges, sconces, portcullises, banding.

__schema30.description: Stair treads and risers. Separate from `floor` because steps are cut pieces that read best with their own tighter texture, and stairs are exactly where a wrong uvScale is most visible.

__schema31.description: Water surfaces, when this location has any. The only optional slot — many dungeons are dry.

hitreg.armor-atlas.name: Armor Atlas
hitreg.armor-atlas.description: Register generated armor artwork against the character UV key, preserve cyan cutouts, and write a game-ready texture atlas.

key.label: UV key
key.description: The flat PNG color-key sheet supplied to the image generator.

art.label: Generated art
art.description: The generated PNG painted over the key layout. It must have exactly the same dimensions as the UV key.

name.label: Output name
name.description: Texture id below assets/textures; folders are allowed. The .png suffix is added automatically.

bleed.label: Bleed
bleed.description: Padding texels dilated around UV islands.

filter.label: Filter
filter.description: Box filtering is the normal downsampling path; nearest preserves hard source pixels.

slices.label: Keep slices
slices.description: Write per-island diagnostic PNGs into the local tool-run record.

artMargin.label: Artwork margin
artMargin.description: Include artwork outside the keyed islands when estimating registration.

skip.label: Skip regions
skip.description: Optional comma-separated island names that are absent from this set, such as hood,ornament.

hitreg.wfc-3d.name: 3D Prefab WFC
hitreg.wfc-3d.description: Collapse a 3D tile grid into a reusable composite prefab. Every occupied cell is a nested prefab instance; the tool never emits raw geometry. Tilesets are hand-authored (exact socket matching) or LEARNED from a modelled kit by tools/wfc-3d/kit.mjs (parts + example structures in, atlased modules + cell prefabs + a tileset with learned face pairs out).

tileset.label: Prefab tileset
tileset.description: JSON describing prefab tiles, their six face sockets, weights, allowed Y rotations, optional boundary sockets, and pinned cells — or a learned tileset written by the kit importer (assets/wfc/<kit>.tileset.json), which adds allowed face pairs, an outside tile and UV-alignment overrides. See tools/wfc-3d/README.md.

name.label: Output prefab
name.description: Prefab id below assets/prefabs; folders are allowed. The .json suffix is added automatically.

height.label: Height (Y)
height.description: Grid cells along world Y. Use 1 for a single-layer layout.

attempts.label: Retry attempts
attempts.description: Fresh deterministic collapses attempted after contradictions.

origin.label: Prefab origin
origin.description: Centered keeps the composite anchor at the bottom-center; minimum starts cell 0 at the anchor.

default.description: Value used when an instance does not set this prop.

bindings.description: Where the value is written on expand: "<localEntityId>/components/<component>/<field>".

description.description: What this knob does, in one line — shown as inspector help and read by agents.

kind.description: Control type. Omit to infer from `default` (and from `options`, which implies enum).

label.description: Human-facing name. Omit to use the prop key.

group.description: Inspector section, e.g. "Handling" or "Damage". Ungrouped knobs come first.

min.description: Inclusive lower bound — with max, renders a slider.

max.description: Inclusive upper bound — with min, renders a slider.

unit.description: Unit suffix shown beside the value: "m", "m/s", "deg", "rpm", "%".

options.description: Allowed values — presence implies an enum dropdown.

assetKind.description: For kind "asset": which library to pick from ("material", "model", "prefab", …).

advanced.description: Hide behind the inspector's “advanced” disclosure; agents still see it.

name.description: Project id. Must match the folder name under projects/, since asset ids namespace by it.

engine.description: Engine version or range this project was built against. Advisory.

tools.description: Registered tools this project needs installed under the engine's tools/ folder.

repo.description: Where to get it — a git URL or other clone/install source. Shown when it is missing.

version.description: Version or range the project was built against. Advisory: nothing enforces it yet.

optional.description: True if the project still runs without it (the tool only regenerates content).

reason.description: What this project uses it for. Worth writing: it is what tells a reader whether they need it.
